Linear PIZZA-31 · bug · Token game · round 3

The real split: pepperoni is pepper + oni, and every option is a verified token

Round 2 feedback (Eva): are you sure all these options are really one token? And why is pepperoni 4, I thought tokens were like syllables.

What changed (4 things)

  1. Checked with a real tokenizer. The gpt-tokenizer package (GPT-4o and GPT-4 encodings) is now a dev dependency, with node scripts/tokens.mjs "any text" to check any copy. Every option in both games is one token: dish · one · soup · hat, order · time · help · socks, ready · hot · late · huge. So is "pizza", by the way; Nina's original worry was wrong.
  2. Screen 1 uses the real split. "pepperoni" is 2 tokens, pepper + oni, not the invented four. The guess tiles still offer 1–4; the right answer is 2. The chopped order is the real eight: I'd · like · a · pepper · oni · , · thanks · !
  3. The screen now says tokens aren't syllables. Under the split: "Why pepper + oni and not syllables? The pieces are whatever showed up most often in the text the model learned from: pepper is a common word, oni a common ending." The chunked-order note says the same in one line.
  4. The ending is rewritten in plain English and matches the real split. In other words: "An AI model doesn't read words. It reads and writes in small pieces called tokens, and you pay for every token: the ones you send and the ones it writes back." What you learned: pepperoni is two (pepper + oni), not a syllable; the order split the same way, even the comma; the bot writes one token at a time. Do: think in tokens, not words; keep chats short when cost matters, you pay for every token in both directions. Don't: count words to guess the cost, a long word can be two or three tokens.
